chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Abdullah al-Kahili said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him about a water channel shared among a group of people, where each man has a known share of water. One of them became independent of his share. He asked: Can he sell it for wheat or barley? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can sell it for whatever he wishes; this is something about which there is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person sell their share of water from a shared channel for grain or other goods?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the principle of unrestricted exchange (ibahah) for water shares, reflecting the practical needs of agrarian communities in early Islamic Iraq. The Imam’s affirmation that one may sell for 'whatever they wish' underscores the flexibility of private property rights in Shia jurisprudence, provided no specific textual prohibition exists. This ruling facilitates economic liquidity in agricultural resources while maintaining the integrity of shared water rights.
